anti_overlap: Does not evaluate the getComputedStyle/MapLibre runtime seam in shadewright-map.ts or its theme-change synchronization — that is fd-cssvar-mapseam-runtime-integrity.
Does not evaluate component-contract reachability, state-precedence logic, or the /plan showcase's wiring of derived states to markup — that is fd-uistatemachine-contract-fidelity.

Focuses on the lint suite (shadewright-lint.ts) as an enforcement mechanism: whether its checks are real, complete, and unevadable — not on whether the underlying canon rules are themselves well-designed.
decision_lens: For each of the nine sw-* checks, construct the minimal edit to the file under test that would make the real canon rule false while leaving the check's regex/string match satisfied (or make the rule hold while the check still fires) — if that edit exists and is small, the check is decorative. Separately, walk every numbered requirement in canon §14 and §0.4's table and confirm a corresponding branch of the lint code actually tests it.
focus: The nine-check §0.4 lint suite (lib/shadewright-lint.ts) as a piece of static-analysis tooling in its own right — whether each check's regex/text-matching implementation actually enforces the canon rule it claims to, or can be satisfied by text that merely resembles compliance (a comment, a stray substring, a value present but unreachable), and which canon rules the suite never touches at all.
name: fd-staticanalysis-tokenlint-evasion
persona: Apply the perspective of a static-analysis and lint-rule engineer who has built regex- and AST-based enforcement tooling for design-token systems and treats every hand-written pattern-match as a claim to be attacked: is there a syntactically different but semantically identical (or semantically different but syntactically identical) input that flips the check's verdict? This reviewer has seen 'contract' tests pass because a docstring happens to mention the right token name, treats a lint suite's own source as more security-sensitive than the code it polices (a broken gate manufactures false confidence at the exact spot everyone stops looking), and reflexively checks whether a text-scanning rule strips comments before it runs.
review_areas: checkStates's runtime-branch detector (`state !== "idle"` / `switch (state)`) and its `data-sw-part=` / `data-sw-state=` presence checks (shadewright-lint.ts ~lines 708-747) run regex directly against raw `f.text`, with NO `stripComments()` pass — unlike checkMotion, checkNoAbsolutes, and checkLogicalProps, which all strip comments first. A component that never actually branches on `state` but ships a comment containing the matching substrings passes `sw-states` with zero real state handling: the keystone check is evadable by a comment, in the same file whose own docstring (lines 181-190) treats comment-triggered false positives as a solved problem for a different check.

The declared-vs-rendered `data-sw-part` matching in checkStates is pure substring/regex over the whole file, not scoped to a reachable code path: a `data-sw-part="foo"` string in a dead branch, an unused template literal, or a part rendered only via the `/plan` page's `?sw-state=` QA override is indistinguishable from a part on every real user path. Nothing distinguishes 'declared and reachable' from 'declared and present in source text only.'

checkRedundancy's component-level heuristic (`mentionsAllBands` + `usesColor` + `hasSecondChannel`, lines ~408-436) is substring-based against the WHOLE file: any of `aria-label|GLYPH|glyph|dashArray|line-dasharray|pattern|title=` appearing ANYWHERE in the file — including code unrelated to the band render — flips `hasSecondChannel` true, so a component could genuinely render the live comfort scale by color alone while an unrelated `title=` attribute elsewhere satisfies the check.

Canon §14 (docs/canon/shadewright.md ~lines 515-527) lists six component-contract requirements, including item 4, 'Both themes (R13.1) and all three breakpoints (R13.5)' — but `checkStates` never inspects a component for dark-mode usage or `wide:`/`compact:`/`regular:` variant coverage, and R6.5's 'their order' (part ordering) is likewise never checked against markup order. A component can be 100% green on `sw-states` while never having been exercised in dark mode or at any non-default breakpoint.

The 'ratchet itself' staleness test (shadewright-lint.test.ts, describe block near the end) only re-runs checkNoAbsolutes/checkLogicalProps/checkMotion/checkRedundancy for stale BASELINE entries — checkContrast, checkClosedSet, checkCitation, and checkStates are asserted `.toEqual([])` directly with no BASELINE filtering anywhere in the test file. If a future contributor adds a BASELINE entry for one of those four (nothing in the code prevents it — BASELINE is just a generic string array), the staleness test would never notice it went unused, silently defeating the ratchet's one stated safety property.

`parseTokens` (the hand-rolled brace/line/comment walker every check depends on) has a single global `inComment`/`selectorStack`/`buffer` state machine; verify it against every token value already in shadewright.tokens.css that contains nested parens, multi-value stacks, or commas (`calc(var(--sw-target-min) + var(--sw-space-3))`, the `-apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, ...` font stack, `rgb(26 22 18 / 0.08)` shadow values) for silent mis-scoping, and consider what a token value containing a literal `{`/`;` inside a future `clamp()`/`min()` expression would do to every downstream check.

severity_examples.condition: A new @shadewright/* component ships with a comment such as `// mirrors ComfortVerdict: switch (state) { ... } and renders data-sw-part="root"` but never actually branches on `state` or emits `data-sw-state`/`data-sw-part` for real. `checkStates` (shadewright-lint.ts ~708-747) matches its regexes against unstripped `f.text`, so this component passes `sw-states` — the canon's stated keystone defense against 'components ship without R11.2 states designed' — while genuinely shipping none of the seven states.
severity_examples.scenario: sw-states's keystone runtime-branch check is satisfiable by a comment alone

severity_examples.condition: docs/canon/shadewright.md's §14 lists 'Both themes (R13.1) and all three breakpoints (R13.5)' as a required part of every component contract, but `checkStates` never inspects for dark-mode-aware styling or `wide:`/`compact:`/`regular:` variant usage anywhere in its ~130 lines of checks (shadewright-lint.ts 680-813). A component contract reports fully green on `sw-states` while having no verified breakpoint or theme coverage at all, and no other one of the eight remaining checks picks up the slack.
severity_examples.scenario: §14's theme/breakpoint contract requirement has zero enforcing check

severity_examples.condition: checkRedundancy's `hasSecondChannel` test (shadewright-lint.ts ~423-426) fires on any occurrence of `title=`, `aria-label`, `glyph`, `dashArray`, or `pattern` anywhere in a component's source, not scoped to the actual band-render call site — a component could render all four comfort bands by color alone in one part of the file and satisfy the redundancy check via a wholly unrelated `title=` attribute elsewhere.
severity_examples.scenario: checkRedundancy's second-channel detector is whole-file substring matching

success_hints: Attempt to write the minimal single-line comment or dead-code addition to each @shadewright/* component that flips sw-states green without changing any rendered behavior; report which checks fall for it and which resist.

Cross-reference §14's six numbered contract requirements (docs/canon/shadewright.md §14) line by line against every branch of checkStates and name any requirement with zero corresponding check — expect at least 'both themes' and 'breakpoints' to be missing; look for others, including part ORDER (R6.5).

Trace parseTokens against every real token value in shadewright.tokens.css containing nested parens/commas/calc()/multi-value stacks and confirm none are mis-scoped before reasoning about hypothetical future values.
Check whether the BASELINE ratchet's staleness test actually covers every check that could plausibly receive a BASELINE-filtered assertion in the future, not just the four it happens to test today.
For every regex-based check in shadewright-lint.ts, ask whether stripComments() runs before the pattern, and if not, construct the comment-only bypass and confirm it actually passes vitest.
task_context: find defects, gaps and false confidence in the Shadewright IMPLEMENTATION (not the canon, already reviewed). Focus: checks that pass vacuously or are trivially evaded; canon rules that NO check enforces; states declared but unreachable; the getComputedStyle token-resolution seam and its failure modes; and anywhere the enforcement suite reports green while the rendered page is wrong — three classes already silently compiled to nothing this session (a bad Tailwind border utility, an undefined `wide:` variant, and an undeclared --color-bg). Weight lib/shadewright-lint.ts and lib/shadewright-lint.test.ts most heavily; treat docs/canon/shadewright.md §0.4 and §14 as the specification the lint suite must be measured against.
